title: Nine traffic deaths in 12 days: Laredo police join TxDOT's End the Streak campaign
excerpt: Two people died Monday morning when a vehicle hit a guardrail on South Mines Road — part of a deadly stretch that has claimed nine lives on Webb County roads in 12 days, according to Laredo police.
content:
Nine people have died in traffic crashes in Webb County in just 12 days, Laredo police say, and the department is joining the Texas Department of Transportation's End the Streak TX campaign to push drivers to make safer choices.

The latest deaths came Monday morning, when a driver and a passenger were killed in a fiery crash after their vehicle hit a guardrail on South Mines Road near Caro Avenue, according to the department.

Laredo Police Chief Miguel Rodriguez joined TxDOT on Monday at the campaign's launch in Laredo, urging drivers to wear a seatbelt, pay attention to the road, and never drive under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

End the Streak TX is TxDOT's statewide campaign to end the streak of daily deaths on Texas roadways. Last year, 4,275 people were killed in traffic crashes across Texas, and this year marks 25 years of daily deaths on Texas roads, according to TxDOT Laredo District Engineer Christopher D. Klug, who called the toll “unacceptable.”

Source: Laredo Police Department, Nov. 10, 2026.
